```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  comment = "#>"
)
source("cache-hook.R")
```

`search_regex()` matches patterns against a text corpus and returns results in KWIC format with inline highlighting. This vignette applies it to politics coverage from the weeks after the 2026 midterms, with three patterns -- age ranges, numeric change expressions, and point margins -- each match returned at the sentence level, ready for close reading or aggregation.

## Sources

The corpus comes from two openly reusable sources: the Pew Research Center politics feed, taken from the bundled `rss_politics` catalog, and The Conversation's US politics feed. Both allow reuse with attribution (The Conversation publishes under CC BY-ND 4.0; Pew Research Center under its terms of use), so the article text can be saved with this vignette. Entries were retrieved in November 2026, in the weeks after the midterm elections; links to every article are kept in the results.

```{r libs, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(textpress)
library(dplyr)
library(DT)
```

```{r web-urls, cache_rds = c("feeds", "web_urls")}
feeds <- c(
  textpress::rss_politics |>
    filter(source == "Pew Research Center") |>
    pull(url),
  "https://theconversation.com/us/politics/articles.atom"
)

web_urls <- textpress::fetch_rss(feeds) |>
  select(-doc_id) |>
  distinct(url, .keep_all = TRUE)
```



## Web text and sentence split

`read_urls()` scrapes and parses the article text; `nlp_split_sentences()` segments each document into analysis-ready sentence rows.

```{r web-text, cache_rds = c("web_text_list", "web_text")}
web_text_list <- web_urls |>
  textpress::read_urls(cores = 4)

web_text <- web_text_list$text |>
  mutate(doc_id = match(url, unique(url))) |>
  relocate(doc_id, .before = 1)
```


Segment each document into sentence rows.

```{r web-ss}
web_ss <- web_text |>
  textpress::nlp_split_sentences(by = c('doc_id', 'node_id'))
```



## Regex patterns

Three patterns: `age_range` matches explicit age constructions; `from_to` captures numeric change expressions; `margin` catches leads and swings stated in points.

```{r patterns}
patterns <- list(
  margin = "\\b\\d{1,2}(?:\\.\\d)?[- ](?:percentage[- ])?points?\\b",
age_range = paste(
  "\\b(?:aged?(?:\\s+between)?|ages?)\\s+\\d{2,3}(?:(?:\\s*(?:[-–]|to|and)\\s*\\d{2,3})|(?:\\s+and\\s+(?:older|younger|over|under)))\\b",
  "\\bunder\\s+\\d{2}(?!\\d|,|%)\\b",
  "\\b\\d{2,3}(?!\\d|,|%)\\s*(?:\\+|and\\s+(?:older|younger|over|under))\\b",
  sep = "|"
),
  from_to   = "\\bfrom\\s+\\d+\\s+to\\s+\\d+\\b"
)
```



## Search results

### Search ~ `age_range`

Sentences containing explicit age ranges or constructions (e.g. *"adults aged 18 to 29"*, *"under 30"*, *"65+"*).

```{r out-age-range}
fs <- web_ss |>
  textpress::search_regex(
    query = patterns$age_range,
    by = c('doc_id', 'node_id'),
    highlight = c('<span style="background:#a6cbe1;">', '</span>')
    )

if (!is.null(fs) && nrow(fs) > 0) {
  fs |>
    distinct(text, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(doc_id, node_id, pattern, text) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
}
```



### Search ~ `from_to`

Sentences with numeric change expressions (e.g. *"from 42 to 51 percent"*) -- useful for tracking shifts in support or turnout figures.

```{r out-from-to}
fs1 <- web_ss |>
  textpress::search_regex(
    query = patterns$from_to,
    by = c('doc_id', 'node_id'),
    highlight = c('<span style="background:#fdc4a8;">', '</span>')
    )

if (!is.null(fs1) && nrow(fs1) > 0) {
  fs1 |>
    distinct(text, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(doc_id, node_id, pattern, text) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
}
```

### Search ~ `margin`

Sentences stating a lead or swing in points (e.g. *"won by 8 points"*, *"a 3.5-percentage-point shift"*) -- the usual way election margins are reported.

```{r out-margin}
fs2 <- web_ss |>
  textpress::search_regex(
    query = patterns$margin,
    by = c('doc_id', 'node_id'),
    highlight = c('<span style="background:#c8e6c9;">', '</span>')
    )

if (!is.null(fs2) && nrow(fs2) > 0) {
  fs2 |>
    distinct(text, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(doc_id, node_id, pattern, text) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
}
```

## Summary

`search_regex()` is best for precise, expressive patterns -- age ranges, numeric constructions, multi-word sequences -- where you control the match exactly. Results come back sentence-level with inline highlighting. For broader vocabulary coverage without hand-crafting every variant, see the dictionary search vignette.
